subject: History
question_text: What is/are the difference/differences between Jagirdar and Zamindar? 1. Jagirdars were holders of land assignments in lieu of judicial and police duties whereas Zamindars were holders of revenue rights without obligation to perform any duty other than revenue collection. 2. Land assignments to Jagirdars were hereditary and revenue rights of Zamindars were not hereditary.
explanation: Jagirdars held land assignments (jagirs) in lieu of judicial and police duties for the state while Zamindars were primarily revenue collectors. The key distinction lies in their administrative responsibilities - Jagirdars had judicial/police duties while Zamindars only collected revenue without other obligations. Both statements correctly describe these differences in the Mughal administrative system.

subject: History
question_text: With reference to land reforms in independent India which one of the following statements is correct?
option_a: The ceiling laws were aimed at family holdings and not individual holdings
option_b: The major aim of land reforms was providing agricultural land to all the landless
option_c: It resulted in cultivation of cash crops as a predominant form of cultivation
option_d: Land reforms permitted no exemptions to the ceiling limits
explanation: The Ceiling on Land Holdings Acts specifically targeted family holdings as deliberate policy choice to keep agricultural units within family control. This was different from individual ceiling limits. Providing land to all landless was not primary aim - it was reducing concentration of land ownership among peasants.

subject: Current Affairs
question_text: The Global Competitiveness Report is published by the
option_b: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
explanation: World Economic Forum publishes Global Competitiveness Report annually since 1979 to rank countries competitive capacity. IMF publishes World Economic Outlook; World Bank publishes Doing Business Report. These are distinct publications with different focuses and methodologies.

subject: History
question_text: Consider the following statements about the Charter Act of 1813: 1. It ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India except for trade in tea and trade with China. 2. It asserted the sovereignty of the British Crown over the Indian territories held by the Company. 3. The revenues of India were now controlled by the British Parliament.
explanation: All three statements are correct: (1) The Act ended EIC monopoly except tea and China trade (2) Asserted Crown sovereignty over Company territories (3) Revenue came under Parliamentary control. This marked the significant shift from company-based to crown rule in India during colonial period.

subject: History
question_text: With reference to Swadeshi Movement consider the following statements: 1. It contributed to the revival of the indigenous artisan crafts and industries. 2. The National Council of Education was established as part of Swadeshi Movement.
explanation: Both statements are correct: (1) Swadeshi revived indigenous crafts and industries particularly textile industry in Bombay presidency (2) National Council of Education was established in 1906 as component of Swadeshi to reduce dependence on colonial education. Movement was multifaceted addressing economic and educational independence.

subject: History
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Movement/Organization - Leader 1. All India Anti-Untouchability League : Mahatma Gandhi 2. All India Kisan Sabha : Swami Sahajanand Saraswati 3. Self-Respect Movement : E. V. Ramaswami Naicker
explanation: All three pairs correctly matched: (1) Gandhi founded All India Anti-Untouchability League (2) Sahajanand Saraswati led All India Kisan Sabha representing peasants (3) E.V.R. Naicker led Self-Respect Movement in Tamil Nadu challenging Brahminical hierarchy. All pioneering social reform movements addressing inequality.

subject: Archaeology
question_text: Which one of the following is not a Harappan site?
explanation: Sohgaura is a Mauryan site not Harappan known for pottery with Ashoka inscriptions. Chanhudaro Kot Diji and Desalpur are confirmed Harappan sites. Sohgaura belongs to Mauryan period much later than Indus Valley Civilization circa 2300-1750 BCE. Proper chronological understanding required.

subject: Archaeology
question_text: In which of the following relief sculpture inscriptions is Ranyo Ashoka (King Ashoka) mentioned along with the stone portrait of Ashoka?
explanation: Sohgaura relief sculpture inscription specifically mentions Ranyo Ashoka along with his stone portrait. This is rare instance where Ashoka portrait appears with inscriptional confirmation providing important evidence about Ashoka appearance and Mauryan administration and self-representation in relief.

subject: Religion
question_text: Consider the following: 1. Deification of the Buddha 2. Treading the path of Bodhisattvas 3. Image worship and rituals
explanation: All three characterize Mahayana Buddhism: (1) Buddha deification - worship as god with divine attributes unlike Theravada (2) Bodhisattva ideal - enlightened beings delay nirvana to help others (3) Image worship and elaborate rituals unlike early Buddhism austere approach. These departures made Buddhism more accessible and ritualistic.

subject: Social History
question_text: With reference to forced labour (Vishti) in India during the Gupta period which one of the following statements is correct?
option_a: It was considered a source of income for the State a sort of tax paid by the people
option_b: It was totally absent in the Madhya Pradesh and Kathiawar regions of the Gupta Empire
option_c: The forced labourer was entitled to weekly wages
option_d: The eldest son of the labourer was sent as the forced labourer
explanation: Vishti was recognized as state income source and tax paid by people through compulsory labor service. Not absent in Gupta heartland. No historical evidence of scheduled wages or hereditary rules for Vishti assignment. Represented state labor extraction mechanism and administrative control.

subject: Architecture
question_text: Building Kalyaana Mandapas was a notable feature in the temple construction in the kingdom of
explanation: Kalyana Mandapa marriage hall became distinctive feature in Chalukya temple design in Deccan region. These structures served as ceremonial halls in temple complexes for important rituals including marriages. Later adopted by other dynasties particularly Vijayanagara in their architectural evolution.

subject: Administration
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. In the revenue administration of Delhi Sultanate the in-charge of revenue collection was known as Amil. 2. The Iqta system of Sultans of Delhi was an ancient indigenous institution. 3. The office of Mir Bakshi came into existence during the reign of Khalji Sultans of Delhi.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct - Amil was revenue officer/collector in Delhi Sultanate. Statement 2 partially debated - Iqta had local precedents but disputed if purely indigenous. Statement 3 incorrect - Mir Bakshi developed during Mughal era not Khalji Sultans. Only 1 definitively correct based on evidence.

subject: Religion
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Saint Nimbarka was a contemporary of Akbar. 2. Saint Kabir was greatly influenced by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
explanation: Both incorrect due to chronological problems: (1) Nimbarka lived 12-13 century while Akbar reigned 16th century - not contemporaries (2) Kabir lived 15th century while Sirhindi lived 16th century - Kabir influenced by earlier Bhakti/Sufi tradition not Sirhindi. Timeline mismatch makes both false and historically inaccurate.

subject: Colonial History
question_text: With reference to the British colonial rule in India consider the following statements: 1. Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in the abolition of the system of indentured labour. 2. In Lord Chelmsford War Conference Mahatma Gandhi did not support the resolution on recruiting Indians for World War. 3. Consequent upon the breaking of Salt Law by Indian people the Indian National Congress was declared illegal by the colonial rulers.
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct: (1) Gandhi opposed indentured labor contributing to abolition (2) Gandhi SUPPORTED WWI recruitment at Chelmsford Conference contrary to this statement - INCORRECT (3) Salt law breaking led Congress declared illegal. Statement 2 wrong so answer A is correct.

subject: Independence Movement
question_text: With reference to Indian National Movement consider the following pairs: Person - Position held 1. Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru : President All India Liberal Federation 2. K. C. Neogy : Member The Constituent Assembly 3. P. C. Joshi : General Secretary Communist Party of India.
explanation: All pairs correctly matched: (1) Sapru was President All India Liberal Federation - moderate reformer (2) Neogy was Constituent Assembly member contributing to Constitution drafting (3) Joshi served as General Secretary Communist Party India. All accurately paired with historical roles and positions.

subject: Culture
question_text: With reference to Mian Tansen which one of the following statements is not correct?
option_a: Tansen was the title given to him by Emperor Akbar
option_b: Tansen composed Dhrupads on Hindu gods and goddesses
option_c: Tansen composed songs on his patrons
explanation: Statement A NOT correct - Tansen was actual real name not title from Akbar. While Akbar honored him elevating to court position Tansen Ramtanu Pandey was not given this name as title by Akbar. Other statements correct - composed sacred Dhrupads courtly songs and created/perfected many ragas in Indian classical music.

subject: Art
question_text: Who among the following Mughal Emperors shifted emphasis from illustrated manuscripts to album and individual portrait?
explanation: Jahangir revolutionized Mughal painting shifting from illustrated manuscripts to individual portraits and personal albums. Under his patronage: personal portraiture became major art form he maintained extensive portrait collections court artists focused on character studies albums (murakkah) were valued highly. Significant stylistic shift.

subject: Geography
question_text: Which one of the following National Parks lies completely in the temperate alpine zone?
explanation: Valley of Flowers in Uttarakhand lies completely in temperate alpine zone at high altitude with: alpine meadows flowering plants high altitude grasslands alpine streams at 3500-4000+ meters. Other parks: Manas tropical Namdapha subtropical Neora Valley subtropical. Only Valley of Flowers entirely temperate alpine.

explanation: Atal Innovation Mission operates under NITI Aayog not ministry. Launched 2016 to promote innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem grassroots innovation technological advancement startup support and innovation centers Atal Tinkering Labs. NITI Aayog serves as planning and policy think tank for government.

option_a: does not set below the horizon at the Arctic Circle
option_b: does not set below the horizon at Antarctic Circle
option_c: shines vertically overhead at noon on the Equator
option_d: shines vertically overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn
explanation: June 21 is summer solstice Northern Hemisphere: sun directly above Tropic of Cancer 23.5 N at Arctic Circle sun does NOT SET midnight sun longest day Northern Hemisphere. Antarctic Circle sun SETS polar night begins winter there. Sun vertical over Tropic Cancer not Capricorn at equinoxes.

subject: History
question_text: Which one of the following groups of plants was domesticated in the New World and introduced into the Old World?
explanation: Correct group tobacco cocoa rubber - all New World crops transforming Old World agriculture and economy. Cotton grown in both regions originally. Coffee originated Africa. Wheat is Old World crop. New World domesticates revolutionized global trade.

subject: Biology
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Asiatic lion is naturally found in India only. 2. Double-humped camel is naturally found in India only. 3. One-horned rhinoceros is naturally found in India only.
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct but 2 wrong: (1) Asiatic lion found only India - Gir Forest true (2) Double-humped camel found Asia-Central Asia Gobi China Mongolia - FALSE (3) One-horned rhino found only India - Kaziranga true. Proper animal distribution knowledge.

subject: Geography

explanation: All matched correctly: (1) Pandharpur-Chandrabhaga sacred site and river (2) Tiruchirappalli-Cauvery actual mapping (3) Hampi-Malaprabha correct pairing. All are actual sacred sites matched with respective rivers proper historical-geographical knowledge.

subject: Economics
question_text: In a given year in India official poverty lines are higher in some States than in others because
option_a: poverty rates vary from State to State
option_b: price levels vary from State to State
option_c: Gross State Product varies from State to State
option_d: quality of public distribution varies from State to State
explanation: Official poverty lines vary between states because PRICE LEVELS differ. Poverty based on consumption levels adjusted for regional price differences. What costs 100 in one state might cost 80-120 in another. This is standard poverty measurement methodology in economics.

subject: Environment
question_text: In the context of which of the following do some scientists suggest the use of cirrus cloud thinning technique and the injection of sulphate aerosol into stratosphere?
option_a: Creating the artificial rains in some regions
option_b: Reducing the frequency and intensity of tropical cyclones
option_c: Reducing the adverse effects of solar wind on the Earth
explanation: These geoengineering techniques proposed to reduce global warming by reflecting sunlight back to space (cloud thinning) or creating cooling aerosols. Both directly address climate change mitigation through stratospheric intervention and atmospheric modification.

subject: Environment
question_text: In the context of which one of the following are the terms pyrolysis and plasma gasification mentioned?
explanation: Pyrolysis and plasma gasification are waste-to-energy conversion technologies converting waste to useful energy by heating without oxygen (pyrolysis) or ionized plasma. Emerging waste management solutions for sustainable resource recovery.

subject: Conservation
question_text: Which of the following are in Agasthyamala Biosphere Reserve?
option_a: Neyyar Peppara and Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve
option_b: Mudumalai Sathyamangalam and Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Silent Valley National Park
option_c: Kaundinya Gundla Brahmeswaram and Papikonda Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Mukurthi National Park
option_d: Kawal and Sri Venkateswara Wildlife Sanctuaries; and Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve
explanation: Agasthyamala Biosphere in Western Ghats of Kerala includes Neyyar Peppara Shendurney Wildlife Sanctuaries and Kalakad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve. Biodiversity hotspot with endemic species in Western Ghats region.

subject: Biology
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Some species of turtles are herbivores. 2. Some species of fish are herbivores. 3. Some species of marine mammals are herbivores. 4. Some species of snakes are viviparous.
explanation: All statements correct: (1) Sea turtles herbivorous - green turtles true (2) Some fish herbivorous - parrotfish true (3) Marine mammals herbivorous - manatees true (4) Snakes viviparous - live birth true. Biological facts supported by evidence.

subject: Wildlife
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Wildlife - Naturally found in 1. Blue-finned Mahseer : Cauvery River 2. Irrawaddy Dolphin : Chambal River 3. Rusty-spotted Cat : Eastern Ghats
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct but 2 wrong: (1) Blue-finned mahseer in Cauvery correct (2) Irrawaddy dolphin in Chambal INCORRECT - found Brahmaputra coastal areas (3) Rusty-spotted cat in Eastern Ghats correct. Proper wildlife distribution knowledge.

subject: Environment
question_text: Why is there a great concern about the microbeads that are released into environment?
option_a: They are considered harmful to marine ecosystems
option_b: They are considered to cause skin cancer in children
option_c: They are small enough to be absorbed by crop plants in irrigated fields
option_d: They are often found to be used as food adulterants
explanation: Microbeads harmful to marine ecosystems because: persist indefinitely consumed by marine life causing bioaccumulation carry toxic chemicals. Banned in many countries. Primary concern marine pollution. Option A is correct main environmental concern.

subject: Botany
question_text: Recently there was a growing awareness in our country about the importance of Himalayan nettle (Girardinia diversifolia) because it is found to be a sustainable source of
explanation: Himalayan nettle sustainable source of textile fiber. Fibers can be used for fabric production similar hemp or jute. Promoted as alternative fiber crop for sustainable textile industry in India.

subject: Remote Sensing
question_text: For the measurement/estimation of which of the following are satellite images/remote sensing data used? 1. Chlorophyll content in the vegetation of a specific location 2. Greenhouse gas emissions from rice paddies of a specific location 3. Land surface temperatures of a specific location
explanation: All three measurable: (1) Chlorophyll via spectral reflectance NDVI (2) Greenhouse gas emissions from large-scale patterns/thermal changes (3) Land surface temperature via thermal bands. Satellite data comprehensive environmental monitoring tool.

subject: Forests
question_text: With reference to the States mentioned above in terms of percentage of forest cover to the total area of State which one of the following is the correct ascending order? [Chhattisgarh Madhya Pradesh Maharashtra Odisha]
explanation: Forest cover ascending order: Maharashtra 3 percent to Madhya Pradesh 31 percent to Chhattisgarh 41 percent to Odisha 43 percent. So 3-2-1-4 is correct sequence from lowest to highest forest cover.

subject: Environment
question_text: Which of the following statements are correct about the deposits of methane hydrate? 1. Global warming might trigger the release of methane gas from these deposits. 2. Large deposits of methane hydrate are found in Arctic Tundra and under the seafloor. 3. Methane in atmosphere oxidizes to carbon dioxide after a decade or two.
explanation: All three correct: (1) Global warming triggers methane release creating feedback loop (2) Large deposits Arctic tundra and seafloor (methane bomb concern) (3) Methane oxidizes CO2 in 1-2 decades in atmosphere. Methane hydrate crucial climate concern.

subject: Environment
question_text: Consider the following: 1. Carbon monoxide 2. Methane 3. Ozone 4. Sulphur dioxide. Which of the above are released into atmosphere due to the burning of crop/biomass residue?
explanation: All four released from biomass burning: (1) CO carbon monoxide (2) Methane (3) Ozone from NOx VOC reactions (4) SO2 sulfur dioxide. Agricultural burning major air pollution source India Punjab region.

subject: Geography
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Sea - Bordering country 1. Adriatic Sea : Albania 2. Black Sea : Croatia 3. Caspian Sea : Kazakhstan 4. Mediterranean Sea : Morocco 5. Red Sea : Syria
explanation: Statements 1 3 and 4 correct but 2 and 5 wrong: (1) Albania borders Adriatic correct (2) Croatia NOT Black Sea - WRONG (3) Caspian-Kazakhstan correct (4) Morocco-Mediterranean correct (5) Syria NOT Red Sea - WRONG directly. Three correct pairs.

subject: Agriculture
question_text: Among the following which one is the largest exporter of rice in the world in the last five years?
explanation: India is world's largest rice exporter with 40 percent market share followed by Vietnam. Both basmati and non-basmati varieties contribute. Vietnam sometimes second depending on year. India dominates global rice exports.

question_text: Consider the following pairs: Glacier - River 1. Bandarpunch : Yamuna 2. Bara Shigri : Chenab 3. Milam : Mandakini 4. Siachen : Nubra 5. Zemu : Manas
explanation: Statements 1 2 and 4 correct: (1) Bandarpunch-Yamuna correct (2) Bara Shigri-Chenab correct (3) Milam-Mandakini INCORRECT (4) Siachen-Nubra correct (5) Zemu-Manas INCORRECT. Three correct pairs identified properly.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In India the use of carbofuran methyl parathion phorate and triazophos is viewed with apprehension. These chemicals are used as
explanation: All four are organophosphate/carbamate PESTICIDES used in agriculture for pest control. They're neurotoxins that inhibit acetylcholinesterase enzyme. Concern about toxicity and persistence in environment and food chain.

subject: Environment
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Under Ramsar Convention it is mandatory on the part of the Government of India to protect and conserve all the wetlands in the territory of India. 2. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2010 were framed by the Government of India based on the recommendations of Ramsar Convention. 3. The Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2010 also encompass the drainage area or catchment regions of the wetlands as determined by the authority.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct but 1 incorrect: (1) Ramsar binding but India can prioritize circumstances NOT mandatory ALL wetlands - INCORRECT (2) 2010 Rules based Ramsar recommendations correct (3) Rules include catchment areas correct. Wetland regulation comprehensive.

subject: Environment
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Agricultural soils release nitrogen oxides into environment. 2. Cattle release ammonia into environment. 3. Poultry industry releases reactive nitrogen compounds into environment.
explanation: All three correct: (1) Agricultural soils release NOx via nitrification-denitrification (2) Cattle release ammonia from manure/digestion (3) Poultry industry releases reactive nitrogen compounds. Nitrogen cycle heavily impacted by agriculture.

subject: Geography
question_text: What is common to the places known as Aliyar Isapur and Kangsabati?
explanation: All three are water reservoir/dam projects: Aliyar Tamil Nadu Isapur dam Kangsabati Jharkhand-West Bengal. Multipurpose water projects - not uranium sites caves or rainforests. Water management infrastructure projects.

subject: Science
question_text: In the context of proposals to the use of hydrogen-enriched CNG (H-CNG) as fuel for buses in public transport consider the following statements: 1. The main advantage of the use of H-CNG is the elimination of carbon monoxide emissions. 2. H-CNG as fuel reduces carbon dioxide and hydrocarbon emissions. 3. Hydrogen up to one-fifth by volume can be blended with CNG as fuel for buses. 4. H-CNG makes the fuel less expensive than CNG.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct: (1) H-CNG reduces CO but doesn't eliminate - INCORRECT (2) Reduces CO2 hydrocarbons correct (3) Up 20 percent hydrogen blend correct (4) NOT less expensive - more costly due hydrogen production - INCORRECT. Answer B correct.

subject: Science
question_text: Why are dewdrops not formed on a cloudy night?
option_a: Clouds absorb the radiation released from the Earth's surface
option_b: Clouds reflect back the Earth's radiation
option_c: The Earth's surface would have low temperature on cloudy nights
option_d: Clouds deflect the blowing wind to ground level
explanation: Correct answer A - clouds absorb outgoing radiation Earth acts like blanket reflects back so surface doesn't cool enough dew formation. Temperature remains above dew point. Clear nights rapid cooling causes condensation and dew formation.

question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an Article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2. explanation: Statement 1 correct - 44th Amendment made PM election non-justiciable. Statement 2 incorrect - Supreme Court hasn't struck down 99th Amendment (relates SC judges collegium). Statement 1 accurate about 44th Amendment placing election beyond judicial review.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes incapacity and proved misbehaviour of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India. 3. The details of the process of impeachment of the Judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968. 4. If the motion for the impeachment of a Judge is taken up for voting the law requires the motion to be backed by each House of the Parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that House and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting.
explanation: Statements 1 3 and 4 correct: (1) Speaker can't reject impeachment motion - correct (3) Details in Judges Inquiry Act - correct (4) 2/3 majority required - correct. Statement 2 wrong - Constitution doesn't exactly define incapacity/misbehavior. Answer D.

question_text: The Ninth Schedule was introduced in the Constitution of India during the prime ministership of
explanation: Ninth Schedule introduced during first PM Jawaharlal Nehru's tenure (1954 via 1st Amendment) to protect land reform laws from judicial review. Later became controversial during Indira Gandhi era with extensive use for various legislation.

subject: Economy
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Coal sector was nationalized by the Government of India under Indira Gandhi. 2. Now coal blocks are allocated on lottery basis. 3. explanation: Only statement 1 correct: (1) Coal nationalized under Indira Gandhi 1973 correct (2) Coal blocks allocated by auction not just lottery - INCORRECT (3) India not fully self-sufficient in coal - still imports some - INCORRECT. Only A correct.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act 1959 exempts several posts from disqualification on the grounds of Office of Profit. 2. The above-mentioned Act was amended five times. 3. The term Office of Profit is well-defined in the Constitution of India.
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correct: (1) Act exempts many posts like judicial educational from office of profit disqualification correct (2) Act amended multiple times (3rd 4th 26th amendments modified) correct (3) Term office of profit NOT precisely defined - vague in Constitution - INCORRECT. Answer A.

subject: Polity
question_text: Under which Schedule of the Constitution of India can the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining be declared null and void?
explanation: Fifth Schedule provides special provisions for tribal administration in India (Scheduled Areas). Transfers of tribal land can be declared null and void under Fifth Schedule protections protecting tribal territorial rights and land holdings.

subject: Social
question_text: Consider the following statements about Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) in India: 1. PVTGs reside in 18 States and one Union Territory. 2. A stagnant or declining population is one of the criteria for determining PVTG status. 3. There are 95 PVTGs officially notified in the country so far. 4. Irular and Konda Reddi tribes are included in the list of PVTGs.
explanation: Statements 2 3 and 4 correct: (1) PVTGs in 18 states/UTs - INCORRECT (more regions) (2) Declining population criterion correct (3) 95 PVTGs officially notified correct (4) Irular and Konda Reddi in PVTG list correct. Option B correct.

subject: Polity
question_text: With reference to the Constitution of India prohibitions or limitations or provisions contained in ordinary laws cannot act as prohibitions or limitations on the constitutional powers under Article 142. It could mean which one of the following?
option_a: The decisions taken by the Election Commission of India while discharging its duties cannot be challenged in any court of law
option_b: The Supreme Court of India is not constrained in the exercise of its powers by laws made by the Parliament
option_c: In the event of grave financial crisis in the country the President of India can declare Financial Emergency without the counsel from the Cabinet
option_d: State Legislatures cannot make laws on certain matters without the concurrence of Union Legislature
explanation: Article 142 Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction not limited by ordinary laws - can do complete justice beyond statutory framework meaning SC has extraordinary powers not limited by Parliamentary legislation.

subject: Polity
question_text: With reference to the Legislative Assembly of a State in India consider the following statements: 1. The Governor makes a customary address to Members of the House at the commencement of the first session of the year. 2. When a State Legislature does not have a rule on a particular matter it follows the Lok Sabha rule on that matter.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct: (1) Governor addresses assembly in first session year - TRUE ceremonial custom (2) When state legislature lacks rule does NOT automatically follow Lok Sabha rules - each state has own rule book - INCORRECT. Answer A.

subject: Global
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Protocol to United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC) has specific provisions for combating transnational organized crime. 2. United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) is the first legally binding universal anti-corruption instrument. 3. United Nations Convention Against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC) has a specific chapter dedicated to returning the assets to the legitimate owners from which they were illegally taken. 4. The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has the mandate to assist in the implementation of both UNCAC and UNTOC.
explanation: Statements 2 3 and 4 correct: (1) UNCAC does NOT have specific protocol on migrant smuggling - INCORRECT (2) UNCAC first legally binding global anti-corruption instrument correct (3) UNTOC has asset recovery chapter correct (4) UNODC mandated assist both conventions - correct. Answer B.

subject: Environment
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Indian Forest Act 1927 has been amended to allow tribals to fell bamboo in forest areas where it grows. 2. Bamboo is classified as minor forest produce under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act 2006. 3. The recognition of forest rights Act 2006 does not prevent the traditional forest dwellers from ownership of minor forest produce.
explanation: All three correct: (1) Indian Forest Act 1927 amendment gave tribals right fell bamboo forest areas (2010) correct (2) Bamboo classified as minor forest produce under 2006 Act correct (3) 2006 Act allows ownership minor forest produce by forest dwellers including bamboo - correct. Comprehensive tribal rights.

subject: Polity
question_text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the right to marry a person of one's choice?
explanation: Article 21 Right to Life includes right to personal liberty which encompasses right to marry person of one's choice (Supreme Court interpretation). Related to human dignity and freedom of choice in personal matters.

subject: Law
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. A biological process to create seed cannot be patented. 2. India has established an Intellectual Property Appellate Board to hear appeals in intellectual property matters. 3. Plant varieties are not eligible for patents but they are eligible for protection under the Plant Varieties Protection Act.
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct: (1) Biological process create seed NOT patentable - seeds/plants not under TRIPS - CORRECT (2) India DOES have IP Appellate Board (established 2014) but NOT main focus here (3) Plant varieties protected under Plant Variety Protection Act not patent - CORRECT. Answer A.

subject: Law
question_text: Environment Protection Act 1986 empowers government to
option_a: Specify and limit activities affecting quality of environment
option_b: Specify and manage processes and handling of hazardous substances
option_c: Set emission or discharge standards for protection
explanation: Environment Protection Act 1986 empowers government to: specify limit activities affecting environment quality manage processes/handling hazardous substances and set emission/discharge standards for pollutants. Comprehensive environmental regulatory authority given to government.

subject: Law
question_text: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 requires
option_a: Segregation of waste into five categories
option_b: Applicability only to notified urban areas
option_c: Specifying criteria for landfill sites as per scientific methods
option_d: Waste cannot move from one district to another
explanation: Rules 2016 provide detailed criteria for landfill sites waste processing facilities. (A) Segregate only 4 categories wet dry hazardous inert (B) Applicable beyond notified areas (C) Exact criteria landfill - CORRECT (D) Waste movement between districts allowed with authorization.

subject: Law
question_text: Industrial Employment Standing Orders Amendment 2018 provides that
option_b: Temporary workers need not be given notice before termination
option_c: Work from home is not allowed
explanation: Both statements 1 and 2 correct: (1) Fixed-term employment makes worker layoff easier (less protection) correct (2) Temporary workers don't need termination notice under amended rules - correct. These amendments reduced worker protections enabling flexibility.

subject: Banking
question_text: Service Area Approach in banks was implemented as part of
explanation: Service Area Approach implemented under Lead Bank Scheme (1974). Each bank designated responsibility for specific geographic areas ensuring credit reach rural areas. Pioneering regional credit allocation policy in banking.

subject: Mining
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Minor minerals are specified by Union Government. 2. Technically minor minerals can be collected by States but Centre makes rules. 3. Any illegal sand mining by States can be done under Court directions.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct: (1) Minor minerals status varies by state - partially - INCORRECT (2) States grant mining leases but center makes rules correct (3) States can frame rules against illegal mining - correct. Proper federalism mineral management.

subject: Economics
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Most of India's external debt is owed by government entities. 2. All external debt is denominated in US dollars.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct: (1) Most external debt owed by government entities - correct (public debt) (2) ALL debt in US dollars - INCORRECT (some in SDR euro yen other currencies). Diverse currency composition external debt.

subject: Banking
question_text: Which one of the following is NOT included in commercial bank assets?
option_d: Money at call and short notice
explanation: Deposits are LIABILITIES not assets for banks (they owe depositors money). Assets are: advances (loans given) investments (securities) money at call (short-term borrowing to other banks). Proper balance sheet accounting.

subject: Economics
question_text: Which of the following help reduce currency crisis risk in India?
option_a: Only IT sector foreign exchange earnings
option_c: IT sector earnings and Remittances from NRIs
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 contribute: (1) IT sector forex earnings major forex builder - correct (2) Government spending increases deficit not reduces crisis - INCORRECT (3) NRI remittances major forex source - correct. Both 1 and 3 strengthen forex position. Answer B (1 and 3).

subject: Polity
question_text: Which of the following commissions/committees recommended that the Governor should be a person outside the State with no intense political involvement in that State?
explanation: Sarkaria Commission (1983) recommended Governor be prominent person from outside state without deep political involvement. Aimed at appointing neutral non-partisan Governors ensuring impartiality in state governance.

subject: Finance
question_text: Participatory Notes are issued to
option_a: Foreign Portfolio Investors wanting Indian stock market entry
explanation: Participatory Notes (PN) issued by registered FPIs to overseas investors enabling indirect market access without direct registration. Commonly used instrument for foreign fund investment in Indian markets.

subject: Environment
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority exists at national and state levels. 2. Public participation in compensatory afforestation is made mandatory under the 2016 Act.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct: (1) CAMFA exists national and state levels correct (2) Public participation in compensatory afforestation NOT mandatory 2016 Act - INCORRECT. Participation encouraged not mandated. Answer A.

subject: Regulation
question_text: Which of the following review the independent regulators in telecommunications insurance electricity and water sectors?
explanation: Parliamentary Department Related Standing Committees (2) and NITI Aayog (5) review independent regulators. Ad-hoc committees (1) case-by-case. Finance Commission (3) fiscal not regulatory. Proper regulatory oversight framework.

subject: Economics
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The 2nd Plan emphasized development of heavy industries and capital goods. 2. The 4th Plan aimed to reduce wealth concentration. 3. The 5th Plan was the first to integrate financial sector.
explanation: All three correct: (1) 2nd Plan emphasized heavy industries (Mahalanobis model) correct (2) 4th Plan aimed reduce wealth concentration - redistribution correct (3) 5th Plan first integrated financial sector planning - correct. Reflects planning evolution.

subject: Global
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. AIIB has over 80 member states. 2. India is the largest shareholder of AIIB. 3. AIIB does not have members from outside Asia.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct: (1) AIIB has 80+ members correct (2) China largest shareholder not India - INCORRECT (India second) (3) AIIB has non-Asian members (Luxembourg UK Germany) - INCORRECT. Only statement 1 accurate.

subject: Banking
question_text: What is the purpose of Inter-Creditor Agreement entered into by Indian banks in respect of accounts ₹50 crore and above?
option_a: To reduce the fiscal deficit burden
option_c: To act as an independent regulator
explanation: Inter-Creditor Agreement aims faster resolution of stressed assets ₹50 crore+ under consortium lending. Enables smoother restructuring when multiple lenders involved in distressed loans. Efficient resolution mechanism.

subject: Banking
question_text: Who selects the chairmen of public sector banks?
explanation: Banks Board Bureau (established 2016) selects PSU bank chairmen through transparent professional process. Replaces earlier single ministry control with professional merit-based selection ensuring competence.

subject: Regulation
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) is the first independent regulatory board set up in India. 2. PNGRB ensures competitive functioning of markets. 3. Appeals against PNGRB orders are heard by Appellate Tribunal for Electricity.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct: (1) PNGRB not first - Telecom Regulatory Authority India 1997 first - INCORRECT (2) PNGRB ensures competitive gas markets correct (3) Appeals go Appellate Tribunal Electricity - correct. Answer B.

subject: Technology
question_text: What is the difference between LTE and VoLTE?
option_a: LTE is marketed as 3G whereas VoLTE is marketed as 3G-enabled voice service
option_b: VoLTE is different technology from LTE
explanation: Neither statement correct: (1) LTE marketed as 4G not 3G; VoLTE as 4G voice-enabled service (2) VoLTE is voice-over-IP technology on LTE not separate technology - same data base. Answer D.

subject: Law
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act 2017 increased paid leave to 3 months before and 3 months after delivery. 2. Crèche visits mandatory 6 times daily. 3. Two-child women get reduced entitlements.
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correct: (1) Paid leave extended 3+3 months (previously 6+6 weeks) correct (2) Crèche visits mandatory 6 times daily correct (3) Two-child women get FULL entitlements NOT reduced - INCORRECT. Answer A.

subject: Economics
question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a sub-index of Ease of Doing Business Index?
explanation: Maintenance of law and order is NOT Ease of Doing Business sub-index. Index focuses economic regulatory aspects: starting business registering property taxes enforcing contracts trading borders insolvency. Not law-order.

subject: Environment
question_text: Extended Producer Responsibility was first introduced in
explanation: Extended Producer Responsibility first introduced Recycled Plastic Rules 1999. Obligates producers manage product lifecycle including waste disposal. Pioneering responsibility concept in India.

subject: Economics
question_text: Economic cost of foodgrains for FCI includes minimum support price and bonus plus
explanation: Economic cost = MSP + Bonus + Procurement incidentals (handling storage marketing) + Distribution cost. Complete accounting all costs procurement distribution centers ensuring transparency.

subject: Polity
question_text: Social capital as part of a country's assets means
option_a: Literacy as a proportion of population
explanation: Social capital refers to societal institutions trust norms networks. Reflects mutual trust social cohesion institutional strength - qualitative aspects enabling collective action and economic development.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. High Courts can declare central laws unconstitutional through judicial review. 2. Supreme Court cannot question constitutional amendments.
explanation: Both incorrect: (1) High Courts CAN declare central laws unconstitutional - yes judicial review (2) Supreme Court CAN question amendments via basic structure doctrine (Kesavananda case). Both powers exist in practice.

subject: Economics
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. PPP is calculated by comparing identical basket of goods across countries. 2. By PPP India is world's 5th-6th largest economy.
explanation: Both correct: (1) PPP calculates comparing identical goods/services adjusting price differences - correct (2) By PPP India world's 5th-6th largest economy - correct. PPP more meaningful living standards comparison than nominal GDP.

subject: Agriculture
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Among kharif crops rice occupies the maximum area. 2. Jowar occupies more area than oilseeds among kharif crops. 3. Cotton always occupies more area than sugarcane. 4. Area under sugarcane cultivation is declining.
explanation: Statements 2 and 4 correct: (1) Rice not max kharif area - maize cotton higher - INCORRECT (2) Jowar area more oilseeds correct (3) Cotton NOT always more sugarcane - varies - INCORRECT (4) Sugarcane area declining water stress - correct. Answer C.

subject: Trade
question_text: Highest value agricultural imports by India in last 5 years
explanation: Vegetable oils account highest import value (~4 billion) for India. Includes palm soybean sunflower oils for consumption industry. Pulses spices also major but oils dominate by value economically significant imports.

subject: Polity
question_text: Most appropriate definition of liberty in the context of polity
explanation: Liberty appropriately means opportunity full self-development within social framework. Positive freedom not just negative freedom from constraints. Aligns liberal political philosophy concept human flourishing and social development.

subject: Technology
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. AR completely shuts out physical world whereas VR does not. 2. VR projects computer images onto real objects. 3. AR keeps you in real world with digital enhancements. 4. VR provides complete immersion in virtual environment.
explanation: Statements 3 and 4 correct: (1) AR NOT complete shutout - overlays digital on real - INCORRECT (2) VR doesn't project on objects - creates immersion - INCORRECT (3) AR keeps in world with enhancements correct (4) VR complete immersion correct. Answer B.

subject: Science
question_text: Denisovan refers to
explanation: Denisovan refers to early human species (Homo denisova) discovered through DNA analysis finger bone in Denisova Cave Siberia. Sister species Neanderthals with distinct genetic lineage. Important human evolution discovery.

subject: Science
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Chromosomes can be constructed from genes of different species. 2. Artificial DNA has been created in laboratory. 3. DNA can replicate outside living cell. 4. Cell divisions take place in petri dishes.
explanation: Statement 3 NOT correct: Artificial functional DNA created in lab YES but DNA must WITHIN cellular machinery or specialized systems to replicate. Cannot independently replicate test tube - needs cellular apparatus or engineered conditions.

subject: Law
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Digital signature is only identification of certifying authority. 2. Digital signature provides proof of user identity for online information access. 3. Digital signature is method of signing electronic documents ensuring non-repudiation.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct: (1) Digital signature NOT just identification - also personal cryptographic process - INCORRECT (2) Proof identity access online information correct (3) Method signing electronic documents non-repudiation - correct. Answer D (2 and 3).

subject: Technology
question_text: Consider the following: 1. Location identification of users. 2. Sleep monitoring. 3. Hearing assistance. Which tasks can be accomplished by wearable devices?
explanation: All three tasks: (1) Location via GPS tracking in smartwatches (2) Sleep monitoring accelerometer heart rate sensors (3) Hearing assistance bone conduction amplification. Wearables comprehensive health monitoring tools.

subject: Science
question_text: Why is RNAi technology gaining popularity?
option_a: 1. Gene silencing therapy development. 2. Cancer treatment development. 3. Hormone replacement therapy development. 4. Virus-resistant crops development.
explanation: A
difficulty: Statements 1 2 and 4 correct: (1) Gene silencing therapy correct (2) Cancer treatment development correct (3) Hormone replacement therapy - INCORRECT (not RNAi use) (4) Virus-resistant crops correct against pathogens. Answer A.

subject: Astronomy
question_text: What is the significance of observing the collision of gravitational waves by laser detectors at extremely long distances like billion light-years away?
explanation: Observation of merging black holes first direct detection of GRAVITATIONAL WAVES (2015 LIGO) confirming Einstein's century-old prediction. Confirms ripples in spacetime fabric from accelerating massive objects.

subject: Medicine
question_text: Consider the following: 1. Genetic predisposition of humans. 2. Incorrect administration of antibiotics. 3. Use of antibiotics in livestock. 4. Multiple chronic disease conditions. Which contribute to multi-drug resistance in India?
explanation: Statements 2 3 and 4 correct: (1) Genetic predisposition NOT primary microbial resistance reason - INCORRECT (though host genetics affects susceptibility) (2) Incorrect antibiotic doses correct (selects resistant) (3) Antibiotics livestock correct (major driver) (4) Chronic diseases predispose infections - correct. Answer D.

subject: Science
question_text: What is Cas9 protein?
explanation: Cas9 is endonuclease protein used as molecular scissors in CRISPR gene editing technology. Cuts DNA specific sequences allowing targeted genetic modifications. Revolutionary gene editing tool.

subject: Medicine
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Hepatitis B is transmitted like HIV. 2. Hepatitis B unlike Hepatitis C has no vaccine. 3. Hepatitis B and C infections greater than HIV globally. 4. Some infected show no symptoms for years.
explanation: Statement B NOT correct: Hepatitis B HAS effective vaccine (since 1981); Hepatitis C does NOT have vaccine. Option B incorrectly reverses vaccine status of two viruses. Other statements accurate.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. In the first Lok Sabha the single largest party in the opposition was the Swatantra Party. 2. In the Lok Sabha a Leader of the Opposition was recognised for the first time in 1969. 3. In the Lok Sabha if a party does not have a minimum of 75 members its leader cannot be recognised as the Leader of the Opposition.
explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect - Socialist Party was largest opposition in first Lok Sabha not Swatantra. Statement 2 is correct - Leader of Opposition first recognized in 1969. Statement 3 is correct - 75 members minimum required. Therefore only statement 2 is correct (option B).

subject: Agriculture
question_text: As per the NSSO 70th Round Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Households consider the following statements: 1. Rajasthan has the highest percentage share of agricultural households among its rural households. 2. Out of the total agricultural households in the country a little over 60 percent belong to OBCs. 3. In Kerala a little over 60 percent of agricultural households reported to have received maximum income from sources other than agricultural activities.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct per NSSO 70th Round survey. Statement 1 is incorrect - Rajasthan does not have highest percentage share of agricultural households. Statements 2 and 3 reflect correct data from the survey.

subject: Environment
question_text: How is the National Green Tribunal (NGT) different from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)? 1. The NGT has been established by an Act whereas the CPCB has been created by an executive order of the Government. 2. The NGT provides environmental justice and helps reduce the burden of litigation in the higher courts whereas the CPCB promotes cleanliness of streams and wells and aims to improve the quality of air in the country.
explanation: Both statements correctly describe differences. NGT established by act addressing environmental disputes; CPCB created by executive order implementing pollution control. NGT reduces court burden by handling environmental cases; CPCB focuses on implementation of pollution standards.

subject: Biology
question_text: Which of the following leaf modifications occur(s) in the desert areas to inhibit water loss? 1. Hard and waxy leaves 2. Tiny leaves 3. Thorns instead of leaves
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct mechanisms. Tiny leaves (2) reduce transpiration surface. Thorns (3) replace leaves eliminating water loss. Hard waxy leaves mentioned but not primary desert adaptation. Answer B correctly identifies mechanisms 2 and 3.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of India. 2. The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. Parliament CAN place laws in Ninth Schedule. Statement 2 oversimplified - while courts had limited power traditionally
difficulty: Supreme Court now allows challenges on basic structure grounds per Kesavananda Saraswati case.

subject: Economics
question_text: Which one of the following best describes the term Merchant Discount Rate sometimes seen in news?
option_a: The incentive given by a bank to a merchant for accepting payments through debit cards pertaining to that bank.
option_b: The amount paid back by banks to their customers when they use debit cards for financial transactions for purchasing goods or services.
option_c: The charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments from his customers through the bank's debit cards.
option_d: The incentive given by the Government to merchants for promoting digital payments by their customers through Point of Sale (POS) machines and debit cards.
explanation: MDR is fee/charge merchants pay banks for accepting debit card payments. Typically percentage of transaction value. Option C correctly defines as charge to merchant not incentive or cashback.

subject: International Relations
question_text: What is/are the consequence/consequences of a country becoming the member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group? 1. It will have access to the latest and most efficient nuclear technologies. 2. It automatically becomes a member of The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT).
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. NSG membership provides access to nuclear technology/fuel. Statement 2 incorrect - NSG membership doesn't automatically make one NPT member. NSG focuses on export controls not membership conditions.

subject: Finance
question_text: With reference to India's decision to levy an equalization tax of 6% on online advertisement services offered by non-resident entities which of the statements is/are correct? 1. It is introduced as a part of the Income Tax Act. 2. Non-resident entities that offer advertisement services in India can claim a tax credit in their home country under the Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.
explanation: Both statements incorrect. Equalization tax levied under Finance Act not Income Tax Act. DTA credit uncertain for this specific tax. Neither statement accurately reflects implementation.

subject: Finance
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Review Committee Report has recommended a debt to GDP ratio of 60% for the general (combined) government by 2023 comprising 40% for the Central Government and 20% for the State Governments. 2. The Central Government has domestic liabilities of 21% of GDP as compared to that of 49% of GDP of the State Governments. 3. As per the Constitution of India it is mandatory for a State to take the Central Government's consent for raising any loan if the former owes any outstanding liabilities to the latter.
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct. FRBM targets accurate for recommended ratios. Constitutional provision requires state consent from Centre if arrears exist. Statement 2 has state liabilities varying by state not just 49%.

subject: Agriculture
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The quantity of imported edible oils is more than the domestic production of edible oils in the last five years. 2. The Government does not impose any customs duty on all the imported edible oils as a special case.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. India imports exceed domestic edible oil production. Statement 2 incorrect - Government DOES impose tariffs/duties on imported oils though rates vary.

subject: History
question_text: He wrote biographies of Mazzini Garibaldi Shivaji and Shrikrishna; stayed in America for some time; and was also elected to the Central Assembly. He was
explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai fits all criteria: wrote those biographies lived in America elected to Central Assembly. Pioneer of Indian nationalism.

subject: Digital Identity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Aadhaar card can be used as a proof of citizenship or domicile. 2. Once issued Aadhaar number cannot be deactivated or omitted by the Issuing Authority.
explanation: Neither statement correct. Aadhaar is identity document not citizenship proof. Aadhaar CAN be cancelled by UIDAI for fraud/misuse.

subject: Geography
question_text: Which of the following has/have shrunk immensely/dried up in the recent past due to human activities? 1. Aral Sea 2. Black Sea 3. Lake Baikal
explanation: Only Aral Sea (1) shrunk dramatically. Black Sea stable not shrinking. Lake Baikal world's deepest freshwater lake not dried. Aral Sea correct example of human-caused environmental disaster.

subject: Governance
question_text: Rule of Law Index is released by which of the following?
option_c: The Office of UN Commissioner for Human Rights
explanation: World Justice Project publishes annual Rule of Law Index assessing governance quality.

subject: Banking
question_text: Which one of the following links all the ATMs in India?
explanation: NPCI operates nationwide ATM network connecting all banks. Also runs UPI and digital payment systems.

subject: Finance
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) is the amount that banks have to maintain in the form of their own funds to offset any loss that banks incur if the account-holders fail to repay dues. 2. CAR is decided by each individual bank.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. CAR is reserve banks must maintain to absorb losses. Statement 2 incorrect - CAR mandated by RBI/regulators not individual banks per Basel III standards.

subject: Technology
question_text: The identity platform Aadhaar provides open Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). What does it imply? 1. It can be integrated into any electronic device. 2. Online authentication using iris is possible.
explanation: Both statements correct. Open API enables integration into various systems. Iris recognition integrated enabling iris-based authentication.

subject: Current Affairs
question_text: Very recently in which of the following countries have lakhs of people either suffered from severe famine/acute malnutrition or died due to starvation caused by war/ethnic conflicts?
explanation: Yemen and South Sudan face severe famines from ongoing conflicts. Angola Zambia Morocco Tunisia Venezuela Colombia have different situations.

subject: History
question_text: Regarding Wood's Dispatch which of the following statements are true? 1. Grants-in-Aid system was introduced. 2. Establishment of universities was recommended. 3. English as a medium of instruction at all levels of education was recommended.
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 true. Grants-in-Aid system introduced. Universities recommended. Statement 3 FALSE - Wood's recommended English as official language but not sole medium at all levels. Local languages encouraged.

subject: Polity
question_text: With reference to the Parliament of India which of the following Parliamentary Committees scrutinizes and reports to the House whether the powers to make regulations rules sub-rules by-laws etc. conferred by the Constitution or delegated by the Parliament are being properly exercised by the Executive within the scope of such delegation?
explanation: Committee on Subordinate Legislation examines delegated legislation ensuring executive stays within Constitutional/Parliamentary authority.

subject: Education
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. As per the Right to Education (RTE) Act to be eligible for appointment as a teacher in a State a person would be required to possess the minimum qualification laid down by the concerned State Council of Teacher Education. 2. As per the RTE Act for teaching primary classes a candidate is required to pass a Teacher Eligibility Test conducted in accordance with the National Council of Teacher Education guidelines. 3. In India more than 90% of teacher education institutions are directly under the State Governments.
explanation: Only statement 2 correct. Teachers must pass TET per NCTE guidelines. Statement 1 oversimplifies - qualifications set nationally/state level. Statement 3 incorrect - mix of private and state institutions.

subject: Culture
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Tradition - State 1. Chapchar Kut festival - Mizoram 2. Khongjom Parba ballad - Manipur 3. Thang-Ta dance - Sikkim
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correct. Chapchar Kut spring harvest festival of Mizoram. Khongjom Parba from Manipur. Thang-Ta traditional martial art from MANIPUR not Sikkim.

subject: Health
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 replaced the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954. 2. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is under the charge of Director General of Health Services in the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. FSSA 2006 did replace PFA 1954. Statement 2 incorrect - FSSAI is autonomous regulatory body not under DG Health Services.

subject: International Relations
question_text: The term two-state solution is sometimes mentioned in the news in the context of the affairs of
explanation: Two-state solution refers to Israel-Palestine conflict resolution creating separate Jewish and Palestinian states.

subject: Food Security
question_text: With reference to the provisions made under the National Food Security Act 2013 consider the following statements: 1. The families coming under the category of below poverty line (BPL) only are eligible to receive subsidised food grains. 2. The eldest woman in a household of age 18 years or above shall be the head of the household for the purpose of issuance of a ration card. 3. Pregnant women and lactating mothers are entitled to a take-home ration of 1600 calories per day during pregnancy and for six months thereafter.
explanation: Only statement 2 correct. NFSA covers APL and BPL not just BPL. Female head household provision correct. Statement 3 incorrect - 1600 calories through ICDS not take-home ration.

subject: Trade
question_text: India enacted The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act 1999 in order to comply with the obligations to
explanation: GI Act 1999 enacted to comply with WTO TRIPS agreement obligations.

subject: Mining
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. In India State Governments do not have the power to auction non-coal mines. 2. Andhra Pradesh and Jharkhand do not have gold mines. 3. Rajasthan has iron ore mines.
explanation: Only statement 3 correct. States DO have power to auction some non-coal minerals. Both AP and Jharkhand have significant mineral resources including gold. Rajasthan major iron ore producer.

subject: Technology
question_text: With reference to digital payments consider the following statements: 1. BHIM app allows the user to transfer money to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account. 2. While a chip-pin debit card has four factors of authentication BHIM app has only two factors of authentication.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. BHIM enables UPI fund transfer. Statement 2 about authentication factors oversimplified/incorrect.

subject: Geography
question_text: Among the following cities which one lies on a longitude closest to that of Delhi?
explanation: Bengaluru lies on approximately same longitude as Delhi.

subject: International Labor
question_text: International Labour Organization's Conventions 138 and 182 are related to
option_b: Adaptation of agricultural practices to global climate change
option_c: Regulation of food prices and food security
explanation: ILO Conventions 138 and 182 specifically address child labor.

subject: Polity
question_text: Regarding Money Bill which of the following statements is not correct?
option_a: A bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions relating to imposition abolition remission alteration or regulation of any tax.
option_b: A Money Bill has provisions for the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India or the Contingency Fund of India.
option_c: A Money Bill is concerned with the appropriation of moneys out of the Contingency Fund of India.
option_d: A Money Bill deals with the regulation of borrowing of money or giving of any guarantee by the Government of India.
explanation: Statement C is NOT correct. Money Bills don't specifically deal with Contingency Fund appropriations alone. Options A B D are correct features of Money Bills.

subject: Polity
question_text: With reference to the election of the President of India consider the following statements: 1. The value of the vote of each MLA varies from State to State. 2. The value of the vote of MPs of the Lok Sabha is more than the value of the vote of MPs of the Rajya Sabha.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. MLAs have different voting values based on state population. Statement 2 incorrect - Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha MPs have equal voting value in presidential election.

subject: Architecture
question_text: The well-known painting Bani Thani belongs to the
explanation: Bani Thani iconic painting belongs to Kishangarh school. Kishangarh developed unique style depicting court lady.

subject: Defense
question_text: What is Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) sometimes seen in the news?
option_d: A defence collaboration between Japan and South Korea
explanation: THAAD is American air defense system developed by Lockheed Martin. Surface-to-air missile system deployed globally.

subject: Culture
question_text: With reference to cultural history of India consider the following statements: 1. Most of the Tyagaraja Kritis are devotional songs in praise of Lord Krishna. 2. Tyagaraja created several new ragas. 3. Annamacharya and Tyagaraja are contemporaries. 4. Annamacharya kirtanas are devotional songs in praise of Lord Venkateshwara.
explanation: Statements 2 3 and 4 correct. Tyagaraja praised Rama not Krishna. Tyagaraja created new ragas. Both 14-15th century composers. Annamacharya composed for Venkateshwara.

subject: Polity
question_text: Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the Rule of Law? 1. Limitation of powers 2. Equality before law 3. People's responsibility to the Government 4. Liberty and civil rights
explanation: Statements 1 2 and 4 are core Rule of Law features. Limitation of powers equality before law liberty/rights are fundamental. Statement 3 reversed - government accountability to people not vice versa.

subject: Economics
question_text: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the meaning of legal tender money?
option_a: The money which is tendered in courts of law to defray the fee of legal cases
option_b: The money which a creditor is under compulsion to accept in settlement of his claims
option_c: The bank money in the form of cheques drafts bills of exchange etc.
option_d: The metallic money in circulation in a country
explanation: Legal tender is money creditor MUST accept by law. Option B correct definition.

subject: Economics
question_text: If a commodity is provided free to the public by the Government then
option_c: the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the tax-paying public.
option_d: the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the Government.
explanation: Even free goods have opportunity cost redistributed from consumers to society through taxes.

subject: Economics
question_text: Increase in absolute and per capita real GNP do not connote a higher level of economic development if
option_a: industrial output fails to keep pace with agricultural output.
option_b: agricultural output fails to keep pace with industrial output.
explanation: True development requires poverty reduction. GNP growth without poverty reduction indicates skewed development.

subject: History
question_text: In the Indian context what is the implication of ratifying the Additional Protocol with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)?
option_a: The civilian nuclear reactors come under IAEA safeguards.
option_b: The military nuclear installations come under the inspection of IAEA.
option_c: The country will have the privilege to buy uranium from the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG).
option_d: The country automatically becomes a member of the NSG.
explanation: Only civilian reactors under IAEA safeguards per protocol. Military installations not inspected. No automatic NSG membership or uranium purchase privilege guaranteed.

subject: Climate
question_text: With reference to the Global Alliance for Climate-Smart Agriculture (GACSA) which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. GACSA is an outcome of the Climate Summit held in Paris in 2015. 2. Membership of GACSA does not create any binding obligations. 3. India was instrumental in the creation of GACSA.
explanation: All statements 1 2 and 3 correct. GACSA emerged from COP21 Paris 2015. No binding obligations on members. India played instrumental role.

subject: Trade
question_text: Consider the following countries: 1. Australia 2. Canada 3. China 4. India 5. Japan 6. USA Which of the above are among the free-trade partners of ASEAN?
explanation: Countries 1 3 4 and 5 are ASEAN free-trade partners. Australia China India and Japan have FTA with ASEAN.

subject: Polity
question_text: Which of the following is/are the aim/aims of Digital India Plan of the Government of India? 1. Formation of India's own Internet companies like China did. 2. Establish a policy framework to encourage overseas multinational corporations that collect Big Data to build their large data centres within our national geographical boundaries. 3. Connect many of our villages to the Internet and bring Wi-Fi to many of our schools public places and major tourist centres.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are aims of Digital India. Connectivity and data centre policy focus correct. Statement 1 not primary aim - not about forming India's own internet companies like China.

subject: Geography
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Towns sometimes mentioned in news - Country 1. Aleppo - Syria 2. Kirkuk - Yemen 3. Mosul - Palestine 4. Mazar-i-sharif - Afghanistan
explanation: Statements 1 and 4 correct. Aleppo in Syria correct. Kirkuk in Iraq not Yemen. Mosul in Iraq not Palestine. Mazar-i-Sharif in Afghanistan correct.

subject: History
question_text: In the Federation established by The Government of India Act of 1935 residuary powers were given to the
explanation: Under 1935 Act residuary powers vested with Governor General centralizing significant authority.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly shall vacate his/her office if he/she ceases to be a member of the Assembly. 2. Whenever the Legislative Assembly is dissolved the Speaker shall vacate his/her office immediately.
explanation: Only statement 1 correct. Speaker must resign if ceases membership. Statement 2 incorrect - automatic vacation but not necessarily immediately upon dissolution.

subject: Polity
question_text: Which one of the following reflects the most appropriate relationship between law and liberty?
option_a: If there are more laws there is less liberty.
option_b: If there are no laws there is no liberty.
option_c: If there is liberty laws have to be made by the people.
option_d: If laws are changed too often liberty is in danger.
explanation: Option B accurately reflects law-liberty relationship. Liberty requires legal framework showing interdependence not inverse relationship.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. No criminal proceedings shall be instituted against the Governor of a State in any court during his term of office. 2. The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of a State shall not be diminished during his term of office.
explanation: Both statements correct. Governor has criminal prosecution immunity during term. Governor's salary/allowances cannot be reduced - constitutional protections for executive independence.

subject: Polity
question_text: Consider the following statements: Human capital formation as a concept is better explained in terms of a process which enables 1. individuals of a country to accumulate more capital. 2. increasing the knowledge skill levels and capacities of the people of the country. 3. accumulation of tangible wealth. 4. accumulation of intangible wealth.
explanation: Statements 2 and 4 correct. Human capital formation about skill/capacity development (2) and intangible wealth accumulation (4) not about physical capital (1) or tangible wealth (3).

subject: Economics
question_text: Despite being a high saving economy capital formation may not result in significant increase in output due to
explanation: High capital-output ratio means capital inefficiently converts to output. Other factors (weak administration illiteracy density) are symptoms not primary cause.

subject: History
question_text: After the Santhal Uprising subsided what was/were the measure/measures taken by the colonial government? 1. The territories called Santhal Paragas were created. 2. It became illegal for a Santhal to transfer land to a non-Santhal.
explanation: Both measures correct. Colonial government created separate Santhal Paragas territory. Land transfer prohibition protected Santhal land rights.

subject: History
question_text: Economically one of the results of the British rule in India in the 19th century was the
option_a: increase in the export of Indian handicrafts
option_b: growth in the number of Indian owned factories
option_d: rapid increase in the urban population
explanation: Commercialization of Indian agriculture was major economic result. British transformed peasant economy to cash crop production for export.

subject: Polity
question_text: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 356 of the Constitution in respect of a particular State then
option_a: the Assembly of the State is automatically dissolved.
option_b: the powers of the Legislature of that State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of the Parliament.
option_c: Article 19 is suspended in that State.
option_d: the President can make laws relating to that State.
explanation: Presidential emergency powers under Article 356 mean state legislature powers exercised by/under Parliament authority. State assembly may continue.

subject: Culture
question_text: Consider the following pairs: Craft - Heritage of 1. Puthukkuli shawls - Tamil Nadu 2. Sujni embroidery - Maharashtra 3. Uppada Jamdani saris - Karnataka
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correct. Puthukkuli shawls from Tamil Nadu. Sujni embroidery from Bihar NOT Maharashtra. Uppada Jamdani from Andhra Pradesh NOT Karnataka.

subject: Technology
question_text: In which of the following areas can GPS technology be used? 1. Mobile phone operations 2. Banking operations 3. Controlling the power grids
explanation: All three are correct GPS applications. Mobile (1) navigation/timing. Banking (2) ATM locations/security. Power grids (3) infrastructure management.

subject: Finance
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Reserve Bank of India manages and services Government of India Securities but not any State Government Securities. 2. Treasury bills are issued by the Government of India and there are no treasury bills issued by the State Governments. 3. Treasury bills offer are issued at a discount from the par value.
explanation: Statements 2 and 3 correct. GOI issues treasury bills at discount. States don't issue treasury bills. Statement 1 incorrect - RBI manages both GOI and state securities.

subject: Science
question_text: Consider the following statements: 1. The Earth's magnetic field has reversed every few hundred thousand years. 2. When the Earth was created more than 4000 million years ago there was 54% oxygen and no carbon dioxide. 3. When living organisms originated they modified the early atmosphere of the Earth.
explanation: Statements 1 and 3 correct. Earth's magnetic field reverses periodically. Living organisms modified early atmosphere. Statement 2 false - early atmosphere had no oxygen.

subject: Technology
question_text: The terms WannaCry Petya and EternalBlue sometimes mentioned in the news recently are related to
explanation: These are famous ransomware/cyber attack tools. WannaCry and Petya are ransomware. EternalBlue is NSA exploit tool.

subject: Agriculture
question_text: With reference to the circumstances in Indian agriculture the concept of Conservation Agriculture assumes significance. Which of the following fall under the Conservation Agriculture? 1. Avoiding the monoculture practices 2. Adopting minimum tillage 3. Avoiding the cultivation of plantation crops 4. Using crop residues to cover soil surface 5. Adopting spatial and temporal crop sequencing/crop rotations
explanation: Statements 2 4 and 5 correct. Minimum tillage reduces soil disturbance. Crop residues cover soil protecting it. Crop rotation maintains fertility. NOT 1 (monoculture sometimes practiced) or 3 (plantation crops acceptable in CA).

subject: Environment
question_text: The term sixth mass extinction/sixth extinction is often mentioned in the news in the context of the discussion of
option_a: Widespread monoculture practices in agriculture and large-scale commercial farming with indiscriminate use of chemicals in many parts of the world that may result in the loss of good native ecosystems.
option_b: Fears of a possible collision of a meteorite with the Earth in the near future in the manner it happened 65 million years ago that caused the mass extinction of many species including those of dinosaurs.
option_c: Large scale cultivation of genetically modified crops in many parts of the world and promoting their cultivation in other parts of the world which may cause the disappearance of good native crop plants and the loss of food biodiversity.
option_d: Mankind's over-exploitation/misuse of natural resources fragmentation/loss of natural habitats destruction of ecosystems pollution and global climate change.
explanation: Sixth extinction refers to human-caused biodiversity loss through overexploitation habitat destruction pollution and climate change. Option D correctly encompasses all these factors.

subject: Space
question_text: With reference to the Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) consider the following statements: 1. IRNSS has three satellites in geostationary and four satellites in geosynchronous orbits. 2. IRNSS covers entire India and about 5500 sq. km beyond its borders. 3. India will have its own satellite navigation system with full global coverage by the middle of 2019.
explanation: Statements 1 and 2 correct. IRNSS constellation has required geostationary/geosynchronous satellites. Covers India and extended area. Statement 3 false - IRNSS regional system not global by 2019.

subject: Science
question_text: Consider the following phenomena: 1. Light is affected by gravity. 2. The Universe is constantly expanding. 3. Matter warps its surrounding space-time. Which of the above is/are the prediction/predictions of Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity often discussed in media?
explanation: All three phenomena predicted by General Relativity. Light bending around massive objects. Universe expansion from Big Bang. Mass-energy warps spacetime geometry.

subject: Agriculture
question_text: With reference to the Genetically Modified mustard (GM mustard) developed in India consider the following statements: 1.
